solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl called on regularly

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the words called on, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A young woman is phoned or visited at frequent intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of CALLED ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleo is a female first name, so it fits a clue asking for some girl.

clue.text: Climber needing a metal spike to get up

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters climb, so they are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nail is a small metal spike hammered into wood

explanation.surface: A mountaineer needs a piton hammered in before going higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns A NAIL backwards, as this is a down entry. 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer but means a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody tropical vine that climbs up trees, a climbing plant.

clue.text: Useless at exploration? It's something more you can ignore

indicators.note: letters that are useless in their present order must be rearranged into something that works

explanation.surface: Someone hopeless at exploring is told a feature is merely an add-on they can skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Useless' rearranges the letters of AT EXPLORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An optional extra is an additional feature, often on a car, that a buyer may decline.

clue.text: Gallivanting more a job for a Biblical king

indicators.note: gallivanting means roaming about, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Roaming around instead of working proves more of a job for an Old Testament monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeroboam was the first ruler of the northern kingdom of Israel in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Yanks with short jackets, not in

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the word in out of the jackets

parts.note: jerkins are short close-fitting jackets, often sleeveless

explanation.surface: Americans wearing short jackets are not at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN from JERKINS. 'Yanks' looks like Americans but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull sharply, the same sudden tug as a jerk.

clue.text: Prude is upset as skirt does?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A prim person is distressed, as a hemline creeps upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt that rides up slides higher on the legs as the wearer moves or sits.

clue.text: Financial statements, awfully late, Ben chases

indicators.note: awfully signals the words are badly treated, scrambled into another order

explanation.surface: Ben, running very late, pursues the company accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance sheet is an accounting statement of assets and liabilities at a given date.

clue.text: Shrubs some azalea can't hide

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener observes that some bushes cannot be concealed by an azalea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to letters in azALEA CAN'T HIde, minus the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthi is a plural of acanthus, a spiny-leaved Mediterranean plant grown in gardens.

clue.text: Mother not drinking before daughter was important

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Mum's staying sober before her daughter's big day really counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that mattered carried weight or significance, so it was important.

clue.text: Boy's letters returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for letters is read in reverse

parts.note: letters delivered by the post are mail

explanation.surface: A lad's correspondence has been sent back to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns MAIL backwards. The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Liam is a common male first name, so it names a boy.

clue.text: Initially pretty averse to one's local dialect

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the next two words, pretty and averse

parts.note: one is I, and one's is the contraction one is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: Someone rather dislikes the way people talk in their own area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes P and A from 'pretty averse'; one's gives I'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Patois is the regional speech of ordinary people, differing from the standard language.

clue.text: Discharge quiet American

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly
US is short for United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken man from the USA is released from duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pus is the thick fluid a wound discharges, so the noun discharge names it.

clue.text: Boy gets a "thank you" for piano piece perhaps

parts.note: a son is a boy child
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A child is thanked for playing something on the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a classical composition, often for solo piano; 'perhaps' admits other instruments.

clue.text: Orchestra pit's, surprisingly, extremely high

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: The musicians' pit below the stage is, oddly, very lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges ORCHESTRA PIT'S, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratosphere is a high layer of the atmosphere, so stratospheric figuratively means very high.

clue.text: Capital of Turkey change from Moscow's hardship

indicators.note: capital here means capital letter, the first letter of the word Turkey

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency, the money used in Moscow

explanation.surface: A tale of Ankara's switch away from a Russian line causing difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Turkey' suggests Ankara, but means its first letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble means difficulty or distress, close in sense to hardship.

clue.text: Regular shape of old cape with label on

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
a tag is a label attached to something

explanation.surface: An antique cloak still has its maker's tag sewn on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' suggests a cloak but is the headland abbreviation C.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular octagon is an eight-sided polygon with equal sides and angles.

clue.text: Potter needs it, prompt!

definitions.meaning: a snooker or pool player who pots balls strikes them with a ...
a signal telling an actor when to speak

explanation.surface: A craftsperson at the wheel urgently demands something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a ceramicist or Harry Potter, but is someone potting balls in snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is both a billiards stick and a prompting signal in theatre.

clue.text: Modus operandi in case causing bother

parts.note: MO is the abbreviation for modus operandi, a way of working
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A criminal's method in a legal case causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' looks like an insertion signal but is the whole meaning of LEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest in its older, milder sense is to pester or annoy someone.

clue.text: To breathe out no longer healthy?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
hale means robustly healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Asks whether struggling to exhale means one is no longer well.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is the verb for expelling air from the lungs.

clue.text: Strayed, I hesitate to say: visibly embarrassed

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation in speech
someone visibly embarrassed goes red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone admits, blushing and hesitant, that they went astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go wrong or wander from the right course, so erred is strayed.

clue.text: I must visit fat Scottish landowner

indicators.note: to visit is to go into a place, so the letter I goes inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: Someone insists they call on a portly Highland estate owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the Scots term for the owner of a large landed estate.

clue.text: Assist Lincoln, maybe, getting close to president

parts.note: Abe is the first name of Abraham Lincoln; 'maybe' marks him as one Abe

indicators.note: close to means the end of, the last letter of president

explanation.surface: Help Lincoln as he approaches the US presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near' but means the final letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Somewhat vulgar denial that can be cultivated

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather crude refusal that could be developed further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' points to letters in vulGAR DENIAl.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardenia is a fragrant flowering shrub, something gardeners grow and cultivate.

clue.text: Got back from a diner, eg, the worse for wear

indicators.note: something the worse for wear is battered out of shape, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone recovered after a café, say, left them looking rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the worse for wear' rearranges A DINER EG.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to get it back after losing it.

clue.text: Team from what we hear sounded weary

indicators.note: this tells us the word for sounded weary is said aloud, matching another spelling

parts.note: to sigh is to breathe out audibly in tiredness

explanation.surface: Apparently the squad let out a tired breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a sports team, especially in British usage.
